*** Update File: AGENTS.md
@@
-- Every endpoint is behind sign-in. Restrict actions with `[RequireRole("...")]`: destructive actions are Admin only, approvals are Approver or Admin.
+- Keep every endpoint behind sign-in. Restrict destructive actions to Admin.
 - Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
 - Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
 - Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
 - Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
 - End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.
 
+## Approval limits (`feature/approval-limits`)
+
+- Let a Manager approve amounts up to and including 50,000.00.
+- Let a Director approve amounts up to and including 500,000.00.
+- Require two distinct approvers above 500,000.00: first a Manager or Director, then a Director.
+- Compare usernames after trimming and ignoring case; never count one user twice.
+- Deny Admin approval; Manager and Director replace Approver.
+- For a denied attempt, throw `ApprovalDeniedException` with an actionable reason; change no fields and do not call `Update`.
+- Test boundaries 50,000.00, 50,000.01, 500,000.00 and 500,000.01.
+- Keep approval rules in `InvoiceApp.Domain`; use no role strings or HTTP types there.
+- Map the session to Domain types in controllers, then call `Handle(...)`.
+- Map `ApprovalDeniedException` in `ApiControllerBase` to `403 { "error": reason }`.
+- Validate first and change state last.
+
 ## Commands
 
 - Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
 - Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
-- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`
+- From `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`, run mutation tests: `dotnet stryker --project InvoiceApp.Domain.csproj` (Stryker 4.13.0).
+- From `e2e`, run end-to-end tests: `npx playwright test`.
 
 ## Demo accounts (not real credentials)
 
-- `demo.approver` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Approver)
+- `demo.manager` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Manager)
+- `demo.director` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Director)
+- `demo.director2` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Director)
 - `demo.admin` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Admin)
 
+## Agent workflow
+
+- Read the Implementer, Test Critic and PR Reviewer skills by path in `.github/skills`.
+- Write the spec first with OpenSpec; handle one task group per prompt.
+- Write tests first; consider a rule done only when a test fails if the rule is removed.
+- Format commits as `<type>(<scope>): <what>` and include a `Why:` line.
+- Let hooks write `docs/ai-log`; never edit it.
+
+## Review expectations
+
+- Report findings in a table: `| ID | Severity | File:line | Finding | Suggested fix |`.
+- Number findings from F-01 upward; use High, Medium or Low severity.
+- Check negative rules assert the invoice is unchanged and all four boundaries are tested.
+- Check nothing changes state before validation and no rule sits in a controller or `app.js`.
+- Check error text is fit for a user.
+
 ## Never
 
 - Commit real credentials, tokens or customer data.
 - Add business logic to `Program.cs` or controllers.
*** End Patch

+# Approval rules
+
+Follow [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md); do not duplicate its guidance.
+
+| Role | Amount band | Outcome |
+|---|---:|---|
+| Manager | ≤ 50,000.00 | May approve as the sole approver |
+| Manager | > 50,000.00 through 500,000.00 | Deny |
+| Manager | > 500,000.00 | May be first approver only |
+| Director | ≤ 500,000.00 | May approve as the sole approver |
+| Director | > 500,000.00 | May be first approver; may be second only if distinct |
+| Admin | Any amount or stage | Deny |
+| Any role | > 500,000.00, second approval | Require a distinct Director; prior Manager or Director is eligible |
+
+Boundaries to test: 50,000.00, 50,000.01, 500,000.00, and 500,000.01.
+Compare usernames after trimming and ignoring case; never count one user twice.
+
+| Case | Expected outcome |
+|---|---|
+| First approver `demo.director`, second `" Demo.Director "` | Deny as the same user |
+| Manager attempts the second approval above 500,000.00 | Deny |
+| Each denial, including boundary and role denials | Assert every invoice field equals its pre-attempt value and `UpdateCount` is 0 |
+
+Test valid distinct Manager→Director and Director→Director approvals above 500,000.00.
+All denial tests must assert both the actionable denial and the unchanged-invoice invariant.

+description: Complete one task group or bug list with a focused test-first change.
+---

+Follow [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md); do not duplicate its guidance.
+
+For one task group or bug list:
+1. Write focused failing tests for the requested behavior.
+2. Run exactly `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln --nologo -v q`.
+3. Show that the tests fail for the expected reason, not a setup or compile error.
+4. Make the smallest change that fixes the behavior.
+5. Run the same suite once more and report its result.
+6. Stop. Do not commit, and do not run the suite again.
+
+If failure is unrelated or not for the expected reason, diagnose it without claiming
+the test-first check passed; fix only what is needed to validate this task.
+Do not silently skip either suite run or report a passing result without its output.

+- Tests added: ...
+- Suite result: ...
+- Files changed: ...
+- Not done: ...

+description: Review the supplied diff for evidence-backed defects without changing files.

+Report only real defects supported by evidence in the diff or relevant context.
+Do not report style, speculation, or recommendations without a defect.
+

+## Why

+### Modified Capabilities
+

+# Spec Delta
+
+## Purpose
+
+Defines amount- and role-based invoice approval, including distinct two-person approval for high-value invoices and clear, non-mutating denial behavior.
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Approval authority is limited by role and amount
+The system SHALL allow Managers to approve invoices up to 50,000.00 and Directors to approve invoices up to 500,000.00, inclusive; only a Director may complete approval above 500,000.00.
+
+#### Scenario: Manager approves 50,000.00
+- **WHEN** a Manager approves an invoice for 50,000.00
+- **THEN** the invoice is approved
+
+#### Scenario: Manager cannot approve 50,000.01
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an invoice for 50,000.01
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice remains unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: Director approves 500,000.00
+- **WHEN** a Director approves an invoice for 500,000.00
+- **THEN** the invoice is approved
+
+#### Scenario: 500,000.01 requires two approvals
+- **WHEN** a Manager or Director approves an invoice for 500,000.01 as the first approver
+- **THEN** the invoice remains PendingApproval and records that approver as the first approver
+
+#### Scenario: Manager is the second approver
+- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to complete approval of an invoice for 500,000.01 after its first approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice remains unchanged
+
+### Requirement: High-value approvals require two distinct approvers
+For an invoice above 500,000.00, the system SHALL require a Manager or Director first and a distinct Director second. Usernames SHALL be compared after trimming and ignoring case.
+
+#### Scenario: The same user cannot approve twice with different casing
+- **WHEN** the first approver attempts a second approval using the same username with different casing or surrounding whitespace
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied and the invoice remains unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Approval denial preserves the invoice and explains the reason
+When an approval attempt is denied, the system SHALL provide an actionable reason and leave every invoice field unchanged.
+
+#### Scenario: Admin attempts approval
+- **WHEN** an Admin attempts to approve an invoice
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with a clear reason and the invoice remains unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: API reports a denied approval
+- **WHEN** an approval attempt is denied through the API
+- **THEN** the response has status 403 and a JSON body containing the denial reason in the `error` field
*** End Patch

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: openspec/changes/add-approval-limits/design.md
+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+See `proposal.md` for motivation and `specs/invoice-approval/spec.md` for behavior. `ApprovalService` currently approves a pending invoice in one operation; the API delegates through `Handle(...)`, and the UI displays request errors.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+- Keep approval policy in the Domain layer and validate the role, amount, and prior approver before changing invoice state.
+- Preserve `PendingApproval` after the first high-value approval and expose the required next approver through the UI.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+- Prevent races between concurrent approval attempts.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Manager and Director replace Approver; Admin cannot approve.** Map the signed-in session to Domain approver types in the controller. This keeps role strings and HTTP concerns out of Domain; retaining a generic Approver role would not express the different limits.
+- **Record the first high-value approver while status remains PendingApproval.** Store `FirstApprovedBy` on the invoice and require a second, distinct Director. This fits the existing lifecycle; adding an intermediate status would change current status handling unnecessarily.
+- **Use Domain `ApprovalDeniedException` for policy denials and map it to HTTP 403 `{ "error": reason }`.** This distinguishes authorization denials from existing 400/404/409 service mappings and gives the UI an actionable message.
+- **Compare usernames after trimming and ignoring case.** This prevents spelling/casing variations from counting the same person twice without requiring a new identity system.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- [Concurrent approvals may race and violate the two-person rule] -> Known risk; concurrency control is out of scope.
+- [Existing approval clients may still use the Approver role] -> Update demo users and approval UI together with the API behavior.
*** End Patch

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: openspec/changes/allow-admin-approval-and-permission-modal/design.md
+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+Approval authority is checked both by the `ApprovalsController` role filter and by `ApprovalService`. The controller currently applies one role filter to approve and reject actions. The static UI handles decision failures in a page-level alert, and the permission-denied text is generated by `RequireRoleAttribute`.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+- Keep the Admin role explicit at the API boundary while applying Director approval rules in the Domain.
+- Present role authorization failures through an accessible, dismissible modal whose state is cleared on session changes.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+- Change Manager or Director limits, self-approval prevention, or high-value approval rules.
+- Grant Admin permission to reject invoices or change the server's permission-denied message.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Apply Director-equivalent limits to Admin in the Domain.** Keep `ApproverRole.Admin` explicit and permit it through the same amount and distinct-approver paths as Director. This avoids translating an Admin identity into a different role at the controller boundary and retains the existing no-HTTP/no-role-string Domain separation. Do not bypass amount or two-person checks.
+- **Scope API authorization to individual actions.** Apply Manager/Director/Admin authorization to approval only and retain the current Manager/Director authorization for rejection. Keeping the controller-level authorization broad enough for both actions would unintentionally grant Admin rejection.
+- **Use an accessible native modal dialog for role-denied feedback.** Detect the existing permission-denied 403 in the UI decision flow and display that message in a dismissible dialog; keep other decision errors in the existing inline error path. Close and clear the dialog when the user dismisses it or the session changes, rather than storing its message in session state.
+- **Test at each boundary.** Add Domain coverage for Admin's Director-limit and distinct-second-approver behavior, API coverage for Admin approval versus Admin rejection, and focused UI/browser coverage for modal opening, dismissal, and session cleanup.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- [Action-level filters can accidentally leave an action unprotected] → Add API tests proving both Admin approval succeeds when eligible and Admin rejection remains forbidden; retain role checks on both actions.
+- [A dialog opened during an asynchronous decision could outlive the session] → Close and clear it from sign-out/session-reset handling, and do not persist permission feedback in storage.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+No data migration or API contract change is required. Deploy the application update normally; rollback by reverting the application change.
*** End Patch

+# Proposal
+
+## Why
+
+Admins cannot currently reject pending invoices, despite the requested rejection workflow. Approve and Reject actions also execute immediately, and a missing rejection reason is reported inline rather than through an error dialog.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- Allow Admins to reject pending invoices when they provide a non-empty reason, without changing existing Manager and Director rejection behavior.
+- Require confirmation before an approval or rejection is submitted.
+- Show an error dialog and do not submit a rejection when its reason is empty or whitespace.
+
+This follow-up supersedes the earlier requirement that Admins cannot reject invoices.
+
+## Capabilities
+
+### New Capabilities
+
+- `invoice-approval`: Define authorized rejection of pending invoices by Admins, with a required reason.
+- `decision-confirmations`: Define confirmation and missing-reason dialogs for approval decisions.
+
+### Modified Capabilities
+
+None. The project has no main OpenSpec capability specs; the related `invoice-approval` behavior is currently described in a completed change delta.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Approval/rejection role authorization in the API.
+- Static approval UI markup and JavaScript for accessible confirmation and error dialogs.
+- Controller and Playwright coverage for Admin rejection, confirmation/cancellation, and missing reasons.
*** End Patch

detail:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: openspec/changes/admin-rejection-and-decision-dialogs/design.md
+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+The reject endpoint permits only Managers and Directors, while approval also permits Admins. The Domain already rejects empty or whitespace-only reasons. The static UI currently submits decisions immediately and reports decision errors inline; it already uses a native `<dialog>` for permission-denied feedback.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+- Add Admin to the reject endpoint's existing role allow-list.
+- Require confirmation for both decisions and show a modal error for an empty rejection reason.
+- Keep declined confirmations and invalid reasons from making API requests.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+- Change invoice lifecycle rules, reason persistence, or existing Manager/Director permissions.
+- Change authorization for any action other than invoice rejection.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Extend only the reject action's role allow-list.** The controller-level `RequireRole` attribute is the authorization point for rejection; adding Admin there fixes the observed denial without moving role policy into the Domain or changing the approve endpoint.
+- **Use native modal dialogs in the existing UI.** Add accessible confirmation and missing-reason dialogs following the existing permission-dialog pattern, rather than browser `confirm()`/`alert()` calls or inline errors. This keeps action behavior consistent with the current accessible dialog and lets cancellation leave the request untouched.
+- **Validate the reason before opening the rejection confirmation.** Treat empty and whitespace-only input as missing, show the error dialog, and make no request. For a non-empty reason, retain the entered value when sending the confirmed rejection.
+- **Cover authorization and user-visible outcomes at their boundaries.** Add a controller test for Admin rejection and focused Playwright tests for confirmed/cancelled decisions and missing-reason feedback.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- [A role change could accidentally expand other permissions] → Change only the Reject action's role attribute and verify the other role restrictions remain intact.
+- [Dialog flow could submit more than once or submit after cancellation] → Keep each confirmation bound to its invoice action and assert pending state after cancellation in Playwright tests.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+No data migration or API contract change is required. Deploy normally; rollback by reverting the application change.
*** End Patch

*** Add File: openspec/changes/add-org-routing/proposal.md
+# Proposal
+
+## Why
+
+Invoices currently have no project ownership, and every signed-in user can see the same invoice and approval lists. This change adds the organization structure needed to route decisions to accountable project and business-unit approvers while limiting invoice creation and visibility to the user's scope.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- Model Business Units, Accounts, Projects, project allocations, Business Unit heads, and optional Delivery Managers (DMs); seed the requested demo organization and users.
+- Require a project for invoice creation and require the creator to be allocated to that project; a project DM counts as allocated.
+- Route invoices by amount and organization role, exclude the requester and lower-ranked candidates, enforce distinct high-value approvers, and use Admin as the specified fallback.
+- Scope approval and invoice lists by Requester, DM, Business Unit head, and Admin; require the current routed approver to approve, while allowing Admin to reject any pending invoice with a reason.
+- Show project, requester, routed approval steps, current wait target, status, and rejection attribution in the UI.
+- Update README and approval guidance, and add tests across the domain, API, and end-to-end UI.
+
+## Capabilities
+
+### New Capabilities
+
+- `organization-directory`: Business Unit > Account > Project hierarchy, heads, DMs, project allocations, and the demo organization.
+- `invoice-approval-routing`: Amount-based approver routing, upward escalation, distinct approval steps, and routed decision permissions.
+- `invoice-access`: Project-restricted invoice creation and role-scoped invoice and approval workspaces.
+
+### Modified Capabilities
+
+None. The repository has no main OpenSpec capability specs; the related approval behavior currently appears only in other change deltas.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Domain invoice and organization models, repository interfaces, routing/decision rules, and in-memory API implementations.
+- API authentication/demo-user data, invoice creation, approvals, and scoped list endpoints.
+- Static UI project selection, approval queue, and invoice table.
+- README and agent approval guidance, plus xUnit and Playwright coverage.
+
+No external database or dependency is required; the application remains an in-memory demo.
*** End Patch

+# Spec Delta
+
+## Purpose
+
+Defines project-based approval routing, upward escalation, distinct approval steps, and who may decide a routed invoice.
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Approval route follows invoice amount and organization roles
+The system SHALL route amounts up to 50,000.00 to the project DM, amounts above 50,000.00 through 500,000.00 to the Business Unit head, and amounts above 500,000.00 to the DM followed by a distinct Business Unit head. If a designated person is unavailable, the system SHALL use the next higher eligible role, with Admin as fallback.
+
+#### Scenario: Low-value invoice routes to the DM
+- **WHEN** a project with a DM submits an invoice for 50,000.00 or less
+- **THEN** the DM is the first routed approver
+
+#### Scenario: Low-value invoice without a DM routes upward
+- **WHEN** a project without a DM submits an invoice for 50,000.00 or less
+- **THEN** the Business Unit head is the first routed approver, or Admin if the head is unavailable
+
+#### Scenario: Mid-value invoice routes to the Business Unit head
+- **WHEN** a project submits an invoice above 50,000.00 and at or below 500,000.00
+- **THEN** its Business Unit head is the first routed approver, or Admin if the head is unavailable
+
+#### Scenario: High-value invoice routes to two distinct people
+- **WHEN** a project with a DM submits an invoice above 500,000.00
+- **THEN** its DM is the first routed approver and its Business Unit head is the second
+
+#### Scenario: High-value invoice without a DM uses the Business Unit head and Admin
+- **WHEN** a project without a DM submits an invoice above 500,000.00
+- **THEN** its Business Unit head is the first routed approver and Admin is the distinct second approver
+
+#### Scenario: Duplicate route assignees are resolved to Admin
+- **WHEN** both high-value approval steps would otherwise be assigned to the same person
+- **THEN** the second step is assigned to a distinct Admin
+
+#### Scenario: No distinct second approver can be assigned
+- **WHEN** no distinct second approver is available after applying the Admin fallback
+- **THEN** the system reports `No second approver available` and leaves the invoice in Draft
+
+### Requirement: Approval routing excludes the requester and lower-ranked people
+The system SHALL NOT route an approval step to the requester or to a person at or below the requester's routing rank. It SHALL move that step upward through DM, Business Unit head, and Admin, in that order.
+
+#### Scenario: Requester is the project DM
+- **WHEN** the requester is the DM assigned for the first approval step
+- **THEN** the first step moves to the Business Unit head or the next higher eligible role
+
+#### Scenario: Requester is the Business Unit head
+- **WHEN** the requester is assigned to a Business Unit head step
+- **THEN** the step moves to Admin
+
+#### Scenario: Escalation keeps high-value approvers distinct
+- **WHEN** upward escalation would assign both high-value steps to one person
+- **THEN** the second step moves to a distinct Admin
+
+### Requirement: Only the current routed approver may approve
+The system SHALL allow approval only by the person currently assigned to the invoice's routed step. Admin SHALL approve an invoice at or below 500,000.00 only when routed to Admin, and MAY complete a high-value second step when routed and distinct from the first approver.
+
+#### Scenario: Current routed approver approves
+- **WHEN** the person assigned to the current step approves a pending invoice
+- **THEN** that step is recorded and the invoice advances to its next routed step or Approved status
+
+#### Scenario: Non-routed person attempts approval
+- **WHEN** a signed-in person who is not assigned to the current step attempts approval
+- **THEN** the attempt is denied with the current required approver identified and the invoice remains unchanged
+
+#

detail:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: openspec/changes/add-org-routing/design.md
+# Design
+
+## Context
+
+See `proposal.md` and the three capability specs. The application is an ASP.NET Core API with a static UI, an in-memory invoice repository, and authentication users configured separately from invoices. `ApprovalService` currently owns invoice lifecycle and amount rules; invoice creation and list filtering are currently in the API controller.
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+**Goals:**
+- Keep organization-based eligibility, routing, and decision rules in Domain code.
+- Make the assigned route available to authorization checks and list views.
+- Enforce project and role scope on the server, not only in the UI.
+- Retain the in-memory demo workflow and existing amount boundaries.
+
+**Non-Goals:**
+- Add persistent storage or an organization-management interface.
+- Change existing amount limits, self-approval protections, or high-value two-person approval.
+- Let Admin bypass the route to approve an invoice at or below 500,000.00.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- **Add Domain organization types and a repository interface, with an in-memory API implementation.** Represent Business Units, Accounts, Projects, and allocations in Domain-facing types; seed the demo hierarchy in the API. This keeps policy independent of storage and avoids a database migration. Keep authentication credentials in the existing user configuration and associate them to organization records by username.
+- **Resolve and snapshot the approver route on submission.** Store the routed first and second usernames separately from actual approval attribution. This makes `Approval 1`, `Approval 2`, and `Waiting on` stable for an in-flight invoice and prevents later organization changes from silently changing who may act. Use the existing first-approval and decision fields for actions actually taken.
+- **Keep lifecycle and routing decisions in Domain services.** Extend the existing approval workflow to assign and enforce routes using the organization directory. Controllers map the signed-in session to Domain identity and translate service outcomes through the existing `Handle(...)` mechanism; they do not choose approvers. A route failure should be detected before leaving Draft and returned as `No second approver available`.
+- **Treat the Admin as a route fallback, not an ordinary route bypass.** A low- or mid-value invoice can be approved by Admin only when routed to Admin; Admin may complete a distinct routed second step above 500,000.00, and may reject any pending invoice with a reason. Other approvals require the current routed identity.
+- **Expose only scoped project choices and lists.** Add a signed-in project-options API for the create form and an approval-list API for pending invoices in the caller's scope plus invoices they decided. Apply the same scope policy to invoice-list API results so hiding a row in JavaScript is never the access-control boundary.
+- **Render identities from directory data.** Use the username as the display name because no separate display names are provided, and format identities as `username (username@example.com)`. Keep existing invoice ID, customer, and amount columns while adding the requested project, requester, routed approvers, waiting target, and rejection attribution.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- [Invoice seeds or existing clients may omit a project] → Update the demo invoice seeds and create request/UI together; reject requests without a valid allocated project.
+- [Requester exclusion and upward escalation could select the same person twice] → Resolve both high-value steps as a pair, enforce distinct normalized usernames, and use Admin for a duplicate second step.
+- [Directory membership may change while invoices are pending] → Snapshot route assignments at submission; current requests and scope checks still use the caller's current identity and organizational access.
+- [A misconfigured organization may not yield a second approver] → Fa

{"path":"C:\Users\Rishab\Desktop\final\ai-sdlc-demo-app\README.md","old_str":"# Invoice Approval Demo App

A small invoice approval app used for live AI-in-SDLC demos. It is deliberately simple: a .NET 8 API, a plain web UI, and an in-memory store, so it runs with one command and no database.

## Run it

```
dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api
```

Open http://localhost:5000 and sign in:

| User | Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo.manager` | `ChangeMe123!` | Manager |
| `demo.manager2` | `ChangeMe123!` | Manager |
| `demo.director` | `ChangeMe123!` | Director |
| `demo.director2` | `ChangeMe123!` | Director |
| `demo.admin` | `ChangeMe123!` | Admin |
| `demo.requester` | `ChangeMe123!` | Requester |
| `demo.requester2` | `ChangeMe123!` | Requester |

These are demo accounts for a local, in-memory app. They are not real credentials.
Each demo identity is displayed with an email address of `<username>@example.com`.

## Organization and routing

The demo organization is:

- BU-DIGITAL (head `demo.director`) > ACC-ACME > PRJ-PORTAL (DM `demo.manager`) and PRJ-MOBILE (DM `demo.manager2`)
- BU-ENTERPRISE (head `demo.director2`) > ACC-GLOBEX > PRJ-ERP (no DM)
- `demo.requester` is allocated to PRJ-PORTAL and PRJ-MOBILE; `demo.requester2` is allocated to PRJ-ERP.

## What it does

1. Create a draft for a project you are allocated to.
2. Submit it for approval. Only the requester who created a draft can submit it.
3. The routed approver approves or rejects it with a reason. Above $500,000, two distinct approvals are required.

Invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, then Approved or Rejected.

Amounts up to and including $50,000 route to the project DM; amounts above $50,000 through $500,000 route to the Business Unit head. Above $500,000, the DM approves first and a distinct Business Unit head approves second. Missing approvers move upward, with Admin as the final fallback. A requester or a person ranked below them is skipped. Admin may approve only when routed to them, and may reject any pending invoice with a reason. Approval and rejection require confirmation; an empty rejection reason displays an error dialog.

The UI shows Submit, Approve and Reject only when the server says the signed-in person may take that action. Approvals are grouped into Pending and Decided. Usernames are matched at sign-in without regard to letter case or surrounding spaces.

Invoice lists are scoped: Requesters see their own invoices, DMs see invoices for their projects, Business Unit heads see invoices in their Business Unit, and Admins see all invoices. Approval lists show pending invoices in the caller's scope and decisions they have made.

## Tests

```
dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln
```

```
  src/InvoiceApp.Api      controllers, sign-in, web UI (wwwroot)
  tests/InvoiceApp.Tests  xUnit tests
docs/use-cases            short feature briefs
AGENTS.md                 conventions for AI coding agents
```
